goal: Apply the Review-time anchor (LEAST(review_date, detected_at), ADR 0019) to the reputation-flavored windows in the dashboard-payload aggregates that owners actually see, extract the anchor fragments into src/lib/kpi/fragments.ts as their single owner, and delete the consumer-less Stack A KPI service + GET /api/dashboard/kpis.
non_goals: Re-anchoring workflow KPIs — response rate (dashboard/service.ts fetchReputationRows, aggregate-queries.ts counter query) and the MonthlyImpactWorker digest stay on detected_at per ADR 0019 D2 (the #675 unanswered-import nudge is deliberate)
Re-anchoring action-timestamp metrics — timeSaved keys on approved_at and does not move
Re-anchoring the recent-review feed (detected_at = ingestion recency, correct) or all-time totals / pending counts
Preserving Stack A's calendar-month volume MoM and TTR-duration metrics — they have never rendered anywhere; the semantics survive in ADR 0019 + CONTEXT.md + the fragment tests
Extracting detectedAtWindowFilter or the TTR validity filter into fragments.ts — both would have zero composers once Stack A dies
Adding an expression index on LEAST(review_date, detected_at) — ADR 0019's no-migration/no-index stance holds; sargability is recorded in the addendum as a deferred note
Fixing the null-vs-0 empty-state divergence between the two stacks (lives in response rate, which is untouched)
Editing historical records — docs/reviews/**/blast-radius.md and the superseded root PLAN.md keep their references to the deleted route
user_visible_behavior: On the single-location dashboard, review velocity, the 8-week sentiment trend, the reputation avg-star current/prior windows, and the 1-5 star rating breakdown bucket imported reviews into their true weeks/windows instead of piling into the import week
On the All-Locations aggregate view, per-location review velocity and rating breakdown bucket on the same anchor
Response rate is unchanged on both views — an imported unanswered review still drags it
The recent-reviews feed is unchanged — imported reviews still surface by ingestion recency
GET /api/dashboard/kpis returns 404 (route deleted); no UI consumed it
invariants: Tenant isolation: every touched query keeps its business_id / account_id predicate written out literally in the query template — fragments never carry a FROM/JOIN or a tenant predicate (ci:tenant-scope reads raw un-evaluated template text)
Windows reach SQL only as bound integers via make_interval(...) — never interpolated text (issue #403)
Invariant #15: dashboard and kpi modules take sql as an explicit parameter and never import @/lib/db/server
Invariant #1: no LLM/external/long-running work moves into Next.js routes
Per-widget degradation survives: a failing re-anchored query still degrades one widget via widgetOrFallback rather than 500ing the dashboard
Sequential-wave dispatch from #767 is preserved — no re-anchor edit may reintroduce a concurrent Promise.all fan-out on the shared pool
One owner per load-bearing spelling: LEAST(review_date, detected_at) is spelled only inside src/lib/kpi/fragments.ts
edge_cases: NULL review_date — LEAST ignores NULLs in Postgres, so the anchor falls back to detected_at
Future-dated review_date (clock skew) — clamps to detected_at; unclamped it lands in a week generate_series never generates and silently vanishes from the trend
aggregate-queries velocity puts the anchor inside a LEFT JOIN ON clause (DATE_TRUNC('week', anchor)::date = gs::date), so the zero-fill per location must still produce a row for every week
Renaming the reviews aliases rv/rev to r in aggregate-queries.ts must not disturb ci:tenant-scope's raw-text scan or collide with the counter query's own r alias (separate statement)
The 45s fail-open Redis caches (dashboard:location:*, the aggregate payload) serve pre-anchor payloads for up to 45s after deploy and after any revert — self-expiring, no invalidation work
Deleting the route leaves scripts/ci/__tests__/db-imports-audit.test.ts asserting composition-root status for a path that no longer exists (string-only test, would pass stale)
Deleting Stack A orphans KpiScope / DashboardKpiSummary / KpiResponseRate / KpiReviewVolume / SentimentTrendPoint in kpi/types.ts while the window vocabulary keeps 9 importers
An imported review older than the selected window drops out of velocity/rating/star entirely — correct under review-time semantics

estimated_prod_lines: 680 changed production lines (~130 added: fragments.ts + plug edits; ~550 deleted: kpi/service.ts 405, kpis/route.ts 91, kpi/types.ts orphans ~50)
estimated_test_lines: 2100 changed test lines (~1060 deleted: kpis route.test 490, kpi service.test 408, service.cache.test 165; ~390 deleted + ~330 rewritten in the re-pointed live-DB anchor suite; ~320 added across the new dashboard/aggregate shape suites and the fragment unit tests)
rollback_plan: No migration and no schema change — revert the PR. The dashboard:location:* and aggregate Redis payloads carry a 45s fail-open TTL and self-expire, so pre-revert re-anchored payloads clear within 45s of the revert deploy with no invalidation step. Restoring GET /api/dashboard/kpis is part of the same revert; it had zero consumers, so nothing external breaks in either direction.
observability: A re-anchored query that throws in prod degrades exactly one widget and raises a Sentry event via reportCaughtError('dashboard/service', ...) with widget: 'velocityRows' | 'ratingBreakdownRows' | 'reputationRows' and degraded: true — the dashboard still renders
The aggregate path raises the same shape under source 'dashboard/aggregate' with widget: 'sliceReviewVelocity' | 'sliceRatingBreakdown'
A 404 rate appearing on /api/dashboard/kpis after deploy would mean an undiscovered consumer existed — expected to stay at zero

KNOWN GAP, stated deliberately: a syntactically valid but semantically wrong anchor emits NO production signal. The live-DB eval suite and the staging smoke (seed an import, confirm the trend spreads across weeks instead of spiking) are the only proof this is correct.
